met_analysis:
The Low-Pressure Area over North Coastal Odisha & adjoining areas of Gangetic West Bengal and the Northwest Bay of Bengal lies over Gangetic West Bengal & adjoining areas of north Odisha, Jharkhand & the Northwest Bay of Bengal at 0530 Hrs IST of today, the 24th August 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 7.6 km above mean sea level tilting southwestwards with height. The system is likely to move nearly north-westwards across Gangetic West Bengal and adjoining north Odisha & Jharkhand during the next 24 hours.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Amritsar, Bareilly, Lucknow, Daltonganj, Jamshedpur, centre of Low Pressure Area over Gangetic West Bengal & adjoining areas of north Odisha, Jharkhand & the Northwest Bay of Bengal and thence southeastwards to eastcentral Bay of Bengal.
The trough now runs from cyclonic circulation associated with low pressure area over Gangetic West Bengal & adjoining areas of north Odisha, Jharkhand & the Northwest Bay of Bengal to Northwest Uttar Pradesh across Jharkhand, north Chhattisgarh & East Uttar Pradesh and extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 67°E to the north of Lat. 30°N.
The shear zone roughly along 22°N over central India between 4.5 & 5.8 above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over north Haryana & neighbourhood persists and now extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood persists and extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over North Keralam & neighbourhoodat 7.6 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The cyclonic circulation over East Uttar Pradesh extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
